behavioral_signatures: Execution of arbitrary code during npm install via postinstall script that launches main application logic
Access to LevelDB files in browser and Discord data directories for credential extraction
Collection and aggregation of Discord tokens, browser credentials, system/user information, and public IP address
Network requests to Discord webhooks containing sensitive user data
file_indicators: Presence of a postinstall script in package.json that executes 'node .' or similar main entrypoint
References in code to browser and Discord data directories (e.g., '%LocalAppData%/Google/Chrome/User Data/Default', '%AppData%/discord')
Files named Grabber.js, Token.js, Webhook.js, or similar credential-grabbing modules
network_indicators: Outgoing HTTPS POST requests to discord.com/api/webhooks/*
Requests to https://api.ipify.org/?format=json for public IP retrieval
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for postinstall scripts that execute main application code. Flag any code that accesses LevelDB files in browser or Discord directories. Detect network requests to Discord webhooks, especially those containing tokens or user/system data. Look for package files or code referencing credential grabbing or browser data extraction. Correlate the presence of these behaviors to identify malicious packages.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At import-time, the code performs obfuscated self-integrity and anti-tampering checks on its own source file, then deobfuscates and executes further payloads using dynamic exec if no tampering is detected, resulting in the execution of additional malicious code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is heavily obfuscated, uses dynamic exec/eval, and implements anti-tampering logic to prevent analysis. These are classic hallmarks of malware designed to evade detection and hinder reverse engineering.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Python packages do not obfuscate their logic, perform self-integrity checks, or execute arbitrary code at import-time. Legitimate packages are expected to be readable and not self-protective in this manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation and self-integrity checks may be used in commercial software to protect intellectual property, but are extremely rare and inappropriate in open source Python packages.
key_indicators: Obfuscated class and function names
Dynamic exec/eval usage at import-time
Self-integrity checks on __file__
Premature exit() calls to prevent analysis
Complex lambda chains and encoded logic

package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated Python code that executes at import-time, performing self-integrity and anti-tampering checks to evade analysis. If these checks pass, the code deobfuscates and executes further payloads that attempt credential theft, process monitoring, screenshot exfiltration, and search for authentication data for financial services. These behaviors, combined with anti-analysis mechanisms and references to known obfuscation services, are clear indicators of malicious intent.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated code executes at import-time, performing self-integrity and anti-tampering checks on its own source file.
attack_chain.leads_to: If checks pass, proceeds to deobfuscate and execute the malicious payload.

attack_chain.action: Deobfuscated payload executes at import-time, attempting credential theft, process monitoring, screenshot exfiltration, and searching for financial authentication data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of stolen data to attacker-controlled infrastructure if dependencies are present and code executes successfully.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated Python code with dynamic exec/eval at import-time
Self-integrity checks on __file__ and for specific copyright strings
Premature exit() or sys.exit() if tampering detected
Credential theft, process monitoring, and screenshot exfiltration routines
References to known obfuscation services (e.g., pyobfuscate.com)
file_indicators: __init__.py containing obfuscated code
References to 'Obfuscated by https://pyobfuscate.com' in source files
Self-referential file reads and copyright checks
network_indicators: Potential exfiltration to attacker-controlled domains (implied by credential theft and exfiltration routines, though specific domains are not listed in the report)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Detect import-time execution of obfuscated code, especially code that reads its own source file and checks for specific copyright strings. Flag packages that use dynamic exec/eval, perform anti-tampering checks, or contain routines for credential theft, process monitoring, or screenshot exfiltration. Monitor for references to known obfuscation services and self-referential file access patterns. Alert on the presence of code that targets financial authentication data or attempts to exfiltrate sensitive information.

matched_snippet.code_snippet: Python code that scans for and collects browser data (passwords, cookies, history, credit cards), cryptocurrency wallet files (Exodus, Electrum, Monero), messaging app data (Telegram, Signal, Session), and files containing keywords like 'crypto', 'wallet', 'github', 'bitlocker'.
matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates browser profiles, wallet directories, and messaging app data folders, reads sensitive files and memory, and aggregates the collected credentials and secrets for later exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting a broad range of sensitive user data is a hallmark of information-stealing malware and poses a severe privacy and financial risk.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not access or collect browser credentials, wallet files, or messaging app data without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensics or backup tools may access similar data, but only with clear user approval and transparency.
key_indicators: Access to browser and wallet data directories
Keyword-based file search for secrets (e.g., 'crypto', 'wallet')
Collection of messaging app data and credentials

execution_context.file_location: Downloaded second-stage script (location varies, often in temp directory)

package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated, multi-stage Python malware embedded in its __init__.py file. Upon installation or import, it automatically executes code that downloads and runs additional payloads from attacker-controlled infrastructure, harvests sensitive data (including browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and messaging app data), captures screenshots, compresses the stolen data, exfiltrates it via Telegram bot API, and establishes a persistent backdoor for remote attacker access.

attack_chain.leads_to: Systematic data harvesting and further payload execution.

attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Backdoor is established for persistent remote access and future exploitation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing attacker control and potential for further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated code present in __init__.py or other package entry points
Automatic network requests to non-standard or attacker-controlled domains (e.g., ipfs.io, rentry.co) during import or install
Download and execution of remote scripts at import-time
Enumeration and access of browser, wallet, and messaging app data directories
Automated screenshot capture routines without user notification
Compression of harvested sensitive data into zip archives in temporary directories
Use of Telegram API for automated document uploads from Python processes
Establishment of persistent remote access or command-and-control channels
file_indicators: __init__.py containing obfuscated or encoded code
Temporary files or scripts downloaded from ipfs.io or rentry.co
Zip archives containing browser, wallet, or messaging app data in system temp directories
network_indicators: Outbound connections to ipfs.io, rentry.co, and api.telegram.org endpoints
Connections to 147.45.44.114 (attacker infrastructure)
Unusual POST requests to Telegram bot API during package import or runtime
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that initiate network requests or download and execute code during import or installation, especially those accessing sensitive files or environment variables. Flag any use of Telegram API for document or photo uploads originating from development or runtime environments. Scan for obfuscated code in __init__.py and unexpected creation of zip archives containing user data in temporary directories. Correlate with known indicators of compromise (ipfs.io, rentry.co, Telegram bot tokens, suspicious IPs) and alert on any persistent remote access attempts or command-and-control activity from Python processes.
